TOMISLAV MESARIĆ
Ulica Lipa 12, 10000 Zagreb, Croatia | +385 1 555 0142 | tomislav.mesaric@example.com

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Butcher and meat counter professional with experience since 2015 in carcass breakdown, meat preparation, customer service and food hygiene. Skilled in cutting and portioning beef, pork and lamb, making fresh sausages, advising customers on cuts and preparation, and maintaining temperature and hygiene records. Holds a vocational butcher certificate and a current HACCP basic food hygiene certificate.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Butcher | Mesnica Kod Ante, family butcher shop, Zagreb | 2019–Present
- Break down 2–3 beef forequarters and 10–12 pork sides per week; bone, trim and portion meat for the counter.
- Prepare four types of fresh sausage to the shop’s recipes; produce approximately 40 kg per week in the busy season.
- Developed the shop’s lamb merguez recipe and adjusted its ćevapi mix to 70% beef and 30% lamb based on customer feedback; the ćevapi won second place at the Zagreb County craft meat fair in 2023.
- Rotate cold-room stock each morning using FIFO, placing older products at the front.
- Record cold-room (0–4 °C) and display-counter temperature checks twice daily.
- Serve approximately 120 customers on a Saturday, advising on cuts and cooking times.
- Train two apprentices in knife handling and cleaning routines.
- Prepare whole lambs and suckling pigs for spit-roasting events, including ordering, butchering, seasoning and delivery. Prepared an order of four lambs and two pigs for a 180-guest wedding in 2024.
- Ran a six-week dry-ageing trial on beef ribs, recording temperature and weight loss; the shop now sells dry-aged rib by pre-order.

Counter Assistant | Tržnica Dolac meat hall stall, Zagreb | 2015–2019
- Served customers, weighed and priced orders, operated the till and completed cash-up.
- Cleaned and sanitised slicers, mincers and the counter at closing.
- Created a closing and cleaning checklist following a market hygiene inspection remark; the checklist remains in use at the stall.

EDUCATION & CERTIFICATES
Vocational Certificate: Butcher, 3-year programme | Food Trades School Zagreb | 2015
HACCP Basic Food Hygiene Certificate | 2021; renewed 2024
Preparing for the Master Butcher exam (majstorski ispit) through the Chamber of Trades | Exam planned for spring 2027; not yet passed

SKILLS
Carcass breakdown (beef, pork and lamb) · Cutting, boning, trimming and portioning · Fresh sausage making · Knife sharpening · Mincer and bandsaw operation · FIFO stock rotation · Cold-chain temperature and hygiene checks · Customer service and product advice · Cash handling · Cleaning and sanitising equipment

LANGUAGES
Croatian (native) · English (good; customer service) · German (basic)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear headings, reverse-chronological experience, quantified production and customer-service achievements, relevant certificates, and practical butcher skills. The content demonstrates both technical capability and the customer-facing qualities FreshCart values, including product advice, reliability, hygiene, FIFO rotation, and temperature recording. The catering, sausage-development, dry-ageing, and inspection-checklist examples add credible impact. The only content concern is the description of the HACCP certificate as “current,” because the supplied information confirms renewal in 2024 but does not explicitly confirm its current validity in 2026.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional section headings, simple text formatting, standard job titles, dates, measurable keywords, and no tables, graphics, columns, or parsing barriers. Relevant terms include “butcher,” “meat counter,” “cutting,” “boning,” “trimming,” “portioning,” “customer service,” “FIFO,” “temperature,” “hygiene,” “HACCP,” “fresh sausage,” and “cash handling.” It should have a very high AI/ATS screening probability for this vacancy because the two mandatory requirements are stated directly and supported by detailed evidence. The document does not claim forklift experience, tray-sealer use, labelling-scale use, or self-service packaging, which is appropriate because those capabilities are not supported by the candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is excellent. The CV shows completed butcher training, nine years of relevant meat-counter/butchery experience, and HACCP knowledge. It directly supports the role’s duties of cutting and portioning fresh meat, advising customers on cuts and preparation, rotating stock using FIFO, and recording temperature checks. It also aligns strongly with FreshCart’s culture through evidence of knowledgeable and honest customer advice, hygiene discipline, reliability, product pride, and practical food-quality improvements. The forklift licence is a nice-to-have gap: the candidate’s notes state that he has no forklift licence, although he has used a hand pallet jack. The CV appropriately does not present this as a qualification. The candidate also has no supermarket, tray-sealer, labelling-scale, or self-service-packaging experience; these are experience gaps rather than defects in the CV.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the Professional Summary, change “Holds a vocational butcher certificate and a current HACCP basic food hygiene certificate” to “Holds a vocational butcher certificate and HACCP Basic Food Hygiene Certificate, renewed in 2024.” This preserves the verified information without asserting current validity that is not explicitly confirmed in the supplied material.

MINOR — In the Education & Certificates section, retain the explicit wording “Exam planned for spring 2027; not yet passed.” This is already correctly written and should not be shortened or presented as a completed qualification.
critique.critical_issues: Potentially unsupported currency claim: the Professional Summary calls the HACCP certificate “current,” while the supplied information confirms that it was renewed in 2024 but does not explicitly confirm its current validity in 2026. Fix by stating the certificate and renewal date without calling it current.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, highly relevant CV with clear reverse-chronological structure, specific production volumes, customer-service metrics, food-safety duties and credible achievement evidence. It is concise, professional and substantially more complete than the original candidate information. The quantified examples—such as 120 Saturday customers, 40 kg of sausage per week and the 180-guest wedding order—make the experience convincing. The preparation for the Master Butcher exam is accurately presented as unfinished, avoiding overstatement.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, conventional formatting, readable bullet points and ATS-friendly text. It includes the main screening terms: butcher, meat counter, carcass breakdown, cutting, portioning, FIFO, HACCP, temperature checks, hygiene, customer service and cash handling. AI/ATS screening probability is high for the stated must-have requirements. The document does not claim unsupported supermarket equipment, self-service packaging or forklift experience. A minor ATS improvement would be to use the exact phrases “completed butcher training,” “HACCP knowledge” and “meat counter assistant” in prominent areas.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is excellent. Completed butcher training and more than two years of meat-counter experience are clearly demonstrated, and HACCP knowledge is supported by the HACCP Basic Food Hygiene Certificate and documented temperature and hygiene checks. The CV closely matches the duties of cutting, portioning, advising customers and FIFO stock rotation, and it supports FreshCart’s culture of product knowledge, honest customer advice, reliability and hygiene. The candidate has no forklift licence, so that nice-to-have is a gap rather than a CV defect. The candidate also has not worked in a supermarket or used tray-sealing and self-service labelling equipment; these are role-context gaps, not reasons to alter the CV with unsupported claims.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ATS ENHANCEMENT: In the Professional Summary, change the opening sentence to: “Butcher and meat counter assistant with completed butcher training and experience since 2015 in carcass breakdown, meat preparation, customer service and HACCP-based food hygiene.” This places the ad’s exact terms near the top without adding unsupported experience.

MINOR ATS ENHANCEMENT: In the Skills section, change “Cold-chain temperature and hygiene checks” to “HACCP knowledge; cold-chain temperature and hygiene checks; FIFO stock rotation.” This makes the must-have HACCP requirement more explicit while remaining supported by the certificate and documented checks.
critique.critical_issues:
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- “maintaining temperature and hygiene records” — the candidate’s material supports temperature records and cleaning/sanitation work, but not maintaining hygiene records.
- “Cold-chain temperature and hygiene checks” — temperature checks are supported, but the candidate’s material does not explicitly support conducting hygiene checks.

“Cold-chain temperature and hygiene checks” — temperature checks are supported, but the candidate’s material does not explicitly support conducting hygiene checks.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, targeted CV with a clear structure, relevant quantified achievements, and credible evidence of butcher and meat-counter experience. It demonstrates carcass breakdown, sausage production, customer advice, hygiene controls, FIFO rotation, temperature logging, apprentice training, and cash handling. The wedding catering, award-winning ćevapi, and dry-ageing trial add useful evidence of initiative and product knowledge. Language is professional and appropriately concise. The only notable content-level weakness is a duplicated skill entry and slightly dense detail in the current-role section.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional section headings, standard employment and education formatting, searchable terms such as “butcher,” “meat counter,” “HACCP,” “cutting,” “boning,” “portioning,” “FIFO,” “temperature checks,” and “customer service,” and no tables, columns, graphics, or unusual symbols that would normally interfere with parsing. Its probability of passing an AI/ATS screen is high because the two core requirements are stated directly and supported by quantified experience. Remove the duplicated “FIFO stock rotation” entry to improve polish and keyword efficiency.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns very strongly with FreshCart’s requirements and culture. It shows completed butcher training, substantially more than two years of meat-counter experience, HACCP knowledge, cutting and portioning, customer advice, FIFO stock rotation, temperature and hygiene records, reliability in busy periods, and pride in product quality. The customer-service evidence supports FreshCart’s “Ask the counter” focus on knowledgeable and honest advice. The candidate’s material does not show a forklift licence, so that nice-to-have is a gap rather than a CV defect. The candidate also has no supermarket, tray-sealer, or self-service labelling experience, and the CV does not claim any; these are not stated requirements and should not be invented. The CV does not specifically demonstrate maintaining a counter at 95% stocked or packaging for self-service shelves, but the underlying job description does not provide candidate evidence for those activities.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR: In the Skills section, delete the second occurrence of “FIFO stock rotation” so the entry appears only once. Keep the stronger combined wording: “HACCP knowledge; cold-chain temperature and hygiene checks; FIFO stock rotation.”

MINOR: In the Professional Experience section under “Butcher | Mesnica Kod Ante,” consider changing “Break down 2–3 beef forequarters and 10–12 pork sides per week; bone, trim and portion meat for the counter” to “Cut, break down, bone, trim and portion 2–3 beef forequarters and 10–12 pork sides per week for the service counter.” This preserves the documented experience while matching the job advertisement’s terms more directly.

- "experience since 2015 in carcass breakdown"
